description: Have a passion in helping communities
summary:
For generations, Filipino farmers have been the backbone of the nation, yet many endure deep-seated struggles, severe hunger, poverty, and systemic government neglect. Today, erratic weather patterns and climate change heavily threaten their livelihoods, making an already fragile existence even more precarious. It is time to help them.

Introducing Smarter Farming with NASA Data by TerraBites, a smart farming app designed to empower those who feed us. Starting in the Philippines before expanding globally, it equips farmers by letting them set their location and utilizing NASA satellite data, weather services, and local info to recommend the best crops. The app suggests protective soil rotations, displays real-time maps of rainfall, temperature, and soil conditions, and features "Siesta," an AI assistant ready to answer agricultural questions.

This also comes with smartphone camera-based soil identification and early warning alerts, such as notifications when there has been no rain for a week, so farmers can act before disaster strikes. TerraBite's app is a vital lifeline against climate and economic hardship, proving that when farmers thrive, the economy thrives.
details:
TerraBite's app is a simple, easy-to-use phone and web app that acts like a smart helper for farmers. All a farmer has to do is type in or point out where their farm is located. Behind the scenes, the app gathers space data from NASA, live weather updates, and local info to figure out the best crops to grow. It shows colorful maps of rain and temperature, suggests ways to keep the soil healthy by rotating crops, and includes a friendly AI helper named "Siesta" to chat with and answer farming questions anytime. It even let farmers check their soil just by taking a picture with their phone camera and send warnings if it hasn’t rained in a week.

The app helps farmers fight back against crazy weather changes caused by climate change. Instead of just guessing when to plant or water, farmers get clear, science-backed advice so they can grow better harvests. It keeps the dirt from wearing out over time and gives every farmer 24/7 access to expert advice right in their pocket. Most importantly, it gives early warnings so farmers can protect their crops before bad weather ruins everything they worked for.

The main goal is to lift Filipino farmers out of poverty and hunger, giving them the respect, support, and stability they have missed out on for so long. By helping them secure their harvests and earn a reliable living, the app makes sure communities have enough food. It is built on a simple belief: when our farmers thrive, the whole country's economy thrives with them.

To build the app, our team used real scientific tools like NASA space data and weather tracking systems. We used popular computer coding languages such as Typescript, CSS, and Java script and map-making software to build the app's features such as GPS and make sure it runs smoothly on mobile phones. For planning, designing, and organizing everything, they used everyday tools like Canva, Google Docs, and Google Drive.

TerraBite takes super complicated and distant science, like pictures and data from space satellites, and turns it into simple, practical tips that any farmer can easily use on their phone. Instead of keeping weather and space data locked away for scientists and government agencies, the app shares it with everyday growers. Plus, adding a friendly AI chat helper named "Siesta" makes learning and getting answers feel like talking to a real person rather than reading a confusing instruction manual.

Our team made sure the app is super simple and friendly to use, even for farmers who aren't used to high-tech gadgets, while also planning for real-life hurdles like poor internet signals in far-off rural areas. We carefully factored in the main environmental elements that directly affect crops, such as weather conditions and soil information. However, because farming involves a massive number of variables, the team set clear limitations (delimitations) by focusing primarily on these weather and soil conditions while setting aside complex biotic factors (like specific pests, plant diseases, or weeds) for this phase. Above all, they kept the real struggles of Filipino farmers, such as hunger, money troubles, and unpredictable weather, at the very heart of the project, ensuring every piece of advice is backed by trusted and accurate science.
